subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
THE IMAGE-WIDE DEMAND CENSUS that claim.WC_commutative-exchange-zero-field-precision-proposal.20260903.v1 asked the integrator to require before commissioning anything. That proposal measured the standing unproven pins plus the shipped value-equality rules and said so verbatim: 'NOT SCREENED IMAGE-WIDE. This is the 6 unproven pins plus the 5 shipped value-equality rules plus this run's 2 new ones, not a sweep of the 2842 paired functions.' This is the sweep. Measured at 24bfa0c5a on a full green build (ninja prints build/GUNE5D/main.dol: OK) with tools/gdl/composed_census/wp_zerofield_census.py, and RE-RUN after the change shipped at dba0a6f48 with identical numbers -- which is the control run the proposal's own 'WHAT A SHIPPED CHANGE WOULD OWE' clause (c) demanded.

METHOD, inherited wholesale from claim.CE_constant-equality-closure-demand-census-image-wide.20260903.v1 with both of its recorded calibration defects carried forward AS FIXES rather than re-discovered. Population: 2845 paired equal-size functions, 288 whose raw body differs from the target. 187 carry a structurally differing word and are out of scope for any relational widening. The remaining 101 are staged raw body -> auto-derived equivalent_copy_form edits -> copy_register_fields, and every one reaches the target bytes under that staging (92 need no form edit, 9 need one or two). DEFECT 1: form sites are detected by DECODED COPY FORM, never by the encoding-level `regfield` label. DEFECT 2, here the FIRST-TRIED PROOF column: apply_patch tries its columns in order and reaches a later one only when the earlier refuses, so every row carries `first_proof` and payoff counts ONLY rows whose first proof is the refinement. STAGING FIDELITY: a pin carrying a permutation, a mask/zero form or its own copy-form edit list is verified by the build over a DIFFERENT intermediate image, so a refusal here says nothing about it; such rows are flagged `staging_replayed: false` and reported as staging artifacts, never as demand. Three columns run over one pair of images: STRICT verify_consistent_recolor; LEGACY, the value-equality relation with the run-44 POSITION-KEYED zero tests seeded with constant equality (the widest configuration that shipped before run 45); SHIPPED, webfrank's current transfer with the same seeding.

A TOOLING NOTE THAT IS PART OF THE RESULT. The run-44 prototype tools/gdl/composed_census/wc_zerofield_probe.py monkey-patched a REFINED transfer beside the shipped one. Once the refinement ships that comparison collapses to shipped-vs-shipped and reads a payoff of ZERO -- which looks exactly like a refutation of the class it justified. The promoted census therefore carries the pre-run-45 transfer verbatim as `legacy_transfer` and scores it against webfrank's current one, so the same table re-runs at any later commit and stays a live regression control instead of decaying into a false negative the day it ships.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: ONE ROW, AND IT IS A SOUNDNESS PAYOFF. first proof = STRICT: 80 rows, customers for nothing. first proof = LEGACY: 9 rows, customers for nothing. first proof = the REFINEMENT: 1 row -- game/pb/pb_texture::fn_800C72DC, 65 insns, tier 1, 0 form edits, proved with 0 substitutions and 0 exchanges, byte-equal, `staging_replayed: true` so this census's staging IS the build's staging for it. Legacy refusal `+0x9c: use of g7 is not value-equal to g28`. It was served by copy_register_fields + unproven_recolor_audit and is now served by copy_register_fields + value_equality_recolor. ZERO staging artifacts, which is the failure mode that cost the CE census three of its five apparent payoff rows. The score payoff is NIL: the function was already byte-equal via its unproven pin, so no percentage moves; what moves is that an unproven pin became a machine proof.

CONTROLS HELD, and the negative half is the load-bearing one. 89 rows are proved by an earlier column and NOT ONE changes its verdict or its declaration counts under the refinement. 11 rows are proved by no column and are the residue any further widening would face: 2 refuse with `base register presence differs (g3 vs g0)` (game/enemy/critter::CritterLoadDone at +0x98, CritterLoadStartNext at +0xe0) and are the LIVE negative control -- the class the RA|0 flag exists for, still failing closed on corpus data rather than only in a fixture; the other 9 refuse on value-equality uses, 4 of them in the FP bank where no RA|0 rule exists at all.

THE UNPROVEN-PIN CROSS-TAB, and a stale count corrected. The proposal called this 'the fourth of the six unproven_recolor_audit rules'; six was the run-44 figure and three had already been retired by run-45 dispatch. Measured over the 154 shipped rules at dba0a6f48, rules resting on unproven_recolor_audit went 3 -> 2. The two survivors are game/audio/mempool::pool_garbage_collect (+0x30 `use of g0 is not value-equal to g0`, a genuine value-to-register assignment difference) and game/world/btricol::PointLineDist2D (+0x30 `use of f0 is not value-equal to f1`, FP bank). Neither is a zero-field artifact and neither moves under any of the four configurations wc_unproven_sweep.py runs.

VERDICT. The census does NOT refute the proposal -- the payoff set is not empty, which is the failure mode claim.law.WF_same-register-both-sides-capability-has-an-empty-payoff-set.20260901.v1 names -- but it confirms the proposal's own honest framing: the payoff is ONE row and it is entirely a soundness payoff. Under the run-45 work order's gate ('build ONLY if payoff >= 2 or it retires an unproven pin') the first disjunct FAILS at 1 and the second SUCCEEDS, and that second disjunct is the whole justification. The shape of the answer matches the CE census's exactly, which is the third independent measurement supporting the general expectation that a focused census over this corpus's relational-widening classes returns a payoff of one.
